subject: economics
chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

concepts.title: Gross Value Added (GVA) Calculation
concepts.definition: A measure of economic output that calculates the value of goods and services produced in an economy after adjusting GDP for subsidies and indirect taxes.
concepts.key_idea: GVA represents the actual value added by producers, obtained by adding subsidies to GDP and subtracting indirect taxes.
question_patterns: calculate the Gross Value Added
what is the GVA if GDP is ... and subsidies are ... and indirect taxes are ...
find the GVA from the given GDP, production subsidies, and indirect taxes
how much is the GVA when GDP is ... with indirect taxes of ... and subsidies of ...
Explain gross value added (gva) calculation in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Add the production subsidies to the Gross Domestic Product
solution_steps.explain: Subsidies increase the value added at producer prices, so they are added to GDP.

solution_steps.action: Subtract indirect taxes from the sum of GDP and subsidies
solution_steps.explain: Indirect taxes are deducted to convert market price valuation to value added at basic prices.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving gross value added (gva) calculation.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Add the production subsidies to the Gross Domestic Product. Step 2: Subtract indirect taxes from the sum of GDP and subsidies. Working: gdp + subsidies, gdp_with_subsidies - indirect_taxes.
worked_examples.answer: Gross Value Added (GVA) Calculation applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply gross value added (gva) calculation to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Add the production subsidies to the Gross Domestic Product. Step 2: Subtract indirect taxes from the sum of GDP and subsidies. Working: gdp + subsidies, gdp_with_subsidies - indirect_taxes.
worked_examples.answer: The method of gross value added (gva) calculation leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Disinvestment Target Achievement
concepts.definition: The quantitative measure of whether the government met, exceeded, or fell short of its annual target for mobilizing capital through selling public sector equity.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the target disinvestment from the actual amount mobilized to evaluate fiscal performance.
question_patterns: calculate the disinvestment surplus or deficit
find the difference between actual disinvestment mobilization and the target
did the government meet its disinvestment target of ... if it mobilized ...
how much more or less did the government mobilize compared to its target of ...
Explain disinvestment target achievement in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Subtract the target disinvestment from the actual mobilized amount
solution_steps.explain: A positive value indicates a surplus (exceeded target), while a negative value indicates a deficit (shortfall).

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving disinvestment target achievement.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Subtract the target disinvestment from the actual mobilized amount. Working: actual_mobilised - target_disinvestment.
worked_examples.answer: Disinvestment Target Achievement applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply disinvestment target achievement to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Subtract the target disinvestment from the actual mobilized amount. Working: actual_mobilised - target_disinvestment.
worked_examples.answer: The method of disinvestment target achievement leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Stabilisation vs Structural Reforms
concepts.definition: The classification of economic reforms into short-term stabilization policies to handle immediate balance of payments and inflation crises, and long-term structural reforms to improve overall economic efficiency.
concepts.key_idea: Stabilisation manages immediate financial crises, while structural reforms restructure the economy for long-term growth.
question_patterns: distinguish between stabilisation and structural reform measures
what are short-term stabilisation measures in NEP
explain the difference between short-term and long-term economic reforms of 1991
classify the reform measures of 1991 into stabilisation and structural
Explain stabilisation vs structural reforms in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Define stabilisation measures as short-term policies focusing on inflation control and foreign exchange reserve maintenance.
solution_steps.explain: These measures aim to correct immediate crises in the balance of payments.

solution_steps.action: Define structural reforms as long-term policies aimed at improving efficiency and removing rigidities.
solution_steps.explain: These include liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation to enhance competitiveness.

concepts.title: Deregulation of Industrial Sector
concepts.definition: The dismantling of regulatory barriers such as industrial licensing, public sector monopoly reservations, and price controls to allow free entry and operation of private firms.
concepts.key_idea: Abolishing licensing and opening up reserved sectors to allow market forces to determine production and pricing.
question_patterns: what were the key steps taken to deregulate the industrial sector in 1991
how did the 1991 reforms change industrial licensing
which industries remained reserved for the public sector after 1991
explain the deregulation of the industrial sector under liberalisation
Explain deregulation of industrial sector in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Check if licensing was abolished for all except a few specified hazardous or strategic industries.
solution_steps.explain: Licensing was retained only for alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronics, aerospace, and drugs.

solution_steps.action: Verify that public sector reservation was restricted to atomic energy and core railway transport.
solution_steps.explain: Most other industries were opened to the private sector, and many goods reserved for small-scale industries were dereserved.

concepts.title: Financial Sector Reforms
concepts.definition: Policy measures designed to transition the role of the central bank from a rigid regulator to a facilitator, encouraging competition through private and foreign bank participation.
concepts.key_idea: Reducing central bank control over interest rates, branch expansion, and lending to encourage private and foreign investment.
question_patterns: what was the major aim of financial sector reforms in 1991
how did the role of RBI change after the 1991 reforms
explain the changes in foreign investment limits in the banking sector
describe the financial sector reforms introduced under liberalisation
Explain financial sector reforms in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Explain how RBI's role transitioned from a strict regulator to a facilitator.
solution_steps.explain: This allowed banks to make many decisions regarding interest rates and branch expansion without prior RBI approval.

solution_steps.action: Note the rise in foreign investment limits and the entry of private and foreign banks.
solution_steps.explain: Foreign investment limits in banks were raised to 74%, and FIIs were allowed to invest in Indian financial markets.

concepts.title: Tax Reforms and Fiscal Policy
concepts.definition: Reforms concerning government taxation and public expenditure policies, aimed at lowering tax rates, simplifying procedures, and introducing unified taxes like GST to improve compliance.
concepts.key_idea: Lowering direct tax rates to encourage voluntary disclosure and compliance, and simplifying indirect taxes (like introducing GST).
question_patterns: what are tax reforms and how do they relate to fiscal policy
why were income and corporation tax rates reduced after 1991
explain the significance of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) introduced in 2016
how did tax reforms aim to reduce tax evasion
Explain tax reforms and fiscal policy in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Describe the continuous reduction in individual income tax and corporation tax rates.
solution_steps.explain: Moderate tax rates discourage tax evasion and encourage voluntary compliance and savings.

solution_steps.action: Describe the simplification of indirect taxes leading up to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in 2016.
solution_steps.explain: GST aims to create a unified national market under the principle of 'one nation, one tax, one market'.

concepts.title: Foreign Exchange Reforms and Devaluation
concepts.definition: The deliberate reduction in the value of the domestic currency relative to foreign currencies to stimulate exports and transition to a market-determined exchange rate system.
concepts.key_idea: Devaluation of the rupee in 1991 to boost exports and foreign exchange inflows, followed by freeing the exchange rate to market forces.
question_patterns: what is devaluation of the rupee and why was it done in 1991
how did foreign exchange reforms resolve the balance of payments crisis
explain how the exchange rate of the rupee is determined post-1991
what was the immediate measure taken in the external sector in 1991
Explain foreign exchange reforms and devaluation in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Explain that the rupee was devalued against foreign currencies in 1991.
solution_steps.explain: This immediate measure was taken to encourage exports and increase the inflow of foreign exchange.

solution_steps.action: Describe the shift from government-controlled exchange rates to market-determined rates.
solution_steps.explain: The value of the rupee is now primarily determined by the demand and supply of foreign exchange in the market.

concepts.title: Trade and Investment Policy Reforms
concepts.definition: The removal of quantitative restrictions on imports and exports, reduction of import tariffs, and dismantling of import licensing to enhance domestic industrial competitiveness.
concepts.key_idea: Removing protectionist trade barriers to increase local industrial efficiency and competitiveness.
concepts.textbook_ref: keec103.txt Section 3.3 (Trade and Investment Policy Reforms)
question_patterns: what were the main objectives of trade and investment policy reforms in 1991
how did the government reform import licensing and quantitative restrictions
why were export duties removed during the 1991 reforms
explain the trade liberalisation measures introduced in India
Explain trade and investment policy reforms in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Explain the abolition of import licensing (except for hazardous/sensitive goods) and quantitative restrictions.
solution_steps.explain: Quantitative restrictions on consumer goods and agricultural products were fully removed by April 2001.

solution_steps.action: Explain the reduction of import tariffs and removal of export duties.
solution_steps.explain: This was done to make domestic industries competitive and boost Indian exports in global markets.

concepts.title: Privatisation and Disinvestment
concepts.definition: The process of reducing government ownership or management in public sector enterprises, either by outright sale or by selling a portion of equity to the public (disinvestment).
concepts.key_idea: Shedding government ownership in public enterprises to improve financial discipline, modernize management, and attract private capital.
question_patterns: what is disinvestment and how does it relate to privatisation
explain the two ways in which government companies are converted into private companies
what was the purpose of selling equity of public sector enterprises
distinguish between privatisation and disinvestment
Explain privatisation and disinvestment in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Explain privatisation as the withdrawal of government ownership/management or outright sale of public companies.
solution_steps.explain: This can be done by selling government equity to the public or private firms.

solution_steps.action: Explain disinvestment as selling a part of the equity of public sector enterprises (PSEs) to the public.
solution_steps.explain: The primary goals are to improve financial discipline, facilitate modernization, and utilize private managerial capabilities.

concepts.title: Globalisation and Outsourcing
concepts.definition: The integration of a country's economy with the global economy, characterized by outsourcing business operations to external nations where skilled labor is available at lower costs.
concepts.key_idea: Creating a borderless world through communication technology, where companies hire external services (like BPOs) from other nations.
question_patterns: what is globalisation and how does it create a borderless world
explain the concept of outsourcing as an outcome of globalisation
why has India become a favorite destination for global outsourcing
what services are commonly outsourced to India
Explain globalisation and outsourcing in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Explain globalisation as the integration of a country's economy with the world economy through networks transcending geographical boundaries.
solution_steps.explain: It aims to increase interdependence and create a borderless world.

solution_steps.action: Explain outsourcing as hiring regular services from external foreign sources.
solution_steps.explain: India is a major outsourcing hub due to low wage rates and a large pool of skilled, English-speaking IT professionals.

concepts.title: World Trade Organisation (WTO) Role
concepts.definition: An international trade organization established in 1995 to succeed GATT, aiming to establish a rule-based, non-discriminatory global trading regime by reducing tariffs and trade barriers.
concepts.key_idea: Promoting free trade by removing tariff and non-tariff barriers and providing equal opportunities to all member nations.
question_patterns: what is the WTO and what are its main objectives
how does the WTO differ from GATT
explain India's role and commitments as a member of the WTO
why do some scholars criticize India's membership in the WTO
Explain world trade organisation (wto) role in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Explain that WTO was founded in 1995 to succeed GATT (established in 1948).
solution_steps.explain: It administers multilateral trade agreements and aims to establish a rule-based trading regime.

solution_steps.action: Detail the goals of reducing tariffs, removing non-tariff barriers, and expanding trade in goods and services.
solution_steps.explain: Critics argue that developed nations dominate trade and maintain protectionist policies while forcing developing nations to open markets.

extracted_variables.subsidies: Total production subsidies provided by the government
